posts.name: Melkhor
posts.cooked: Ouch! That got way closer than it had any right to be. It looked like I was cruising towards an easy win with everyone still standing when the Ennead suddenly unleashed Hell (or rather, Duat, I suppose) on me. I still got the Mint in the end, but only Fanatic (who got saved by her Aegis) and Haka (with 4 HP left) were still standing at the end. A good reminder never to count out the Ennead completely, and a personal reminder of just why I -hate- Ruins of Atlantis as an environment so very, very much!

posts.name: jajd2c
posts.cooked:
Mint. Barely.

I was setup & in good shape when Don't Dismiss Anything pulled End of Days & wiped my ongoings and equipment. The Ennead took advantage of that & started cleaning up my heroes. NightMist fell first, followed quickly by Ra and Fanatic. Haka held out for a while but could not stand versus the onslaught from the Ennead. Finally, the Scholar stood alone versus 5 of the Ennead, gravely wounded, and bolstered only by the memory of his fallen comrades.

And he kept standing there, getting healing & card draws from his fallen allies. The Ennead's incap effects kept his deck cycling so that he had Flesh to Iron always up, 1 to 3 Mortal Flesh to Energy most turns, and a Solid to Liquid up about half the time. The various incap heal effects kept damage going on the Ennead, barely outstripping their combined heals for a while, but eventually gaining enough momentum to take them out one by one. And in accordance with the intro for this one-shot, a Kraken got the final blow in, finishing Gen and the Ennead.

It was a long, slow war of attrition, and took about an hour to complete. It's the first time in a long while I've had all 9 of the Ennead come out without playing on advanced. Rough one, but a fun game nonetheless.

posts.name: bolnerap
posts.cooked:
Very quick and easy Mint here.  Never saw Set or Geb, and there were only 5 cards in the Ennead trash at endgame.
 
Fanatic (12 HP) - Absolution first for damage, then Divine Focus got played off-turn by Atlantean Font of Power while she still had Prayer of Desperation in her hand.  So, I burned almost all my cards, played Prayer, and burned some more. Good solid match.
 
Haka (15 HP) - Taiaha and dumped his hand for Toxic Seaweed. Dominion got played off-turn by Atlantean Font of Power, which helped fuel one final hit with Haka of Battle.
 
Nightmist (9 HP) - Stunlocked Ennead for a couple rounds with Mistbound, including the round with the aforementioned Atlantean Font of Power to no Villain effect.
 
Ra (17 HP) - Got out the staff and blew it up, got another Staff, played and consistently used Drawn to the Flame, and Living Conflagration got played off-turn. Omnomnom damage.
 
Scholar (30 HP) - Truth seeker every round, Flesh to Iron stayed out the whole game, and used Get Out of the Way and Grace Under Fire each once to great effect.
 
Atlantis: KO'd Tox Seaweed as soon as I saw it. Mystical Defenses helped more than it hurt, as did Hallway Collapse and Font of Power. Never saw Phosphorescent Chamber, Kraken, or Leaking Room.

posts.name: mightyschoop
posts.cooked:
Near mint and an easier time the second time around. Took out Nuit first, then focused on Atum, to take out the second card play that he can trigger. Saved Shu for a later hit to prevent the extra environment draws.
Didn’t bother with Flesh of the Sun God this time.

With the extra shuffles, the Random Number God was kinder to me this time as I did not get hit with multiple Leaking Rooms or Ancient Magics.

Couple of fun plays- rigged Nightmist to fire an Oblivion with a 4/2 combo while my team was protected by Scholar’s Alchemical Redirection and Flesh to Iron.
Don’t Dismiss Anything played Solar Flare out of turn, allowing Ra to pump 8 damage into each surviving Ennead member to end the game. (Scorched Earth and Drawn to the Flame, Staff of Ra in play.)

posts.name: schadkehnfreude
posts.cooked:
Ennead is usually a fun romp that's challenging but not enough to represent imminent doom and this was no different.

Due to the variance of Nuit shuffling the environment deck (obviously we killed her first) my results aren't that replicable but on turn 4 the game swung decisively when I got a Phosphorescent Chamber.  Ennead zaps us for 6 or whatever and then I unload on them with buffed damage and Nightmist uses Mistbound to prevent them from retalitating next turn.  End of turn 5, we get ANOTHER Phosphorescent Chamber so I'm at +2 damage.  Ennead does nothing, Haka Rampages, Misty Oblivions, Scholar spits Proverbs for another round of damage powers and the Kraken finishes the lone surviving Ennead off.
